Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{{x}^{2}}=|x|
$$

Also, we notice that $9$ and ${a}^{2}$ are both perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{9{a}^{2}} & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}\cdot {a}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3\cdot 3\cdot a\cdot a} \\  & =\sqrt{3\cdot a\cdot 3\cdot a} \\  & =\sqrt{3a\cdot 3a} \\  & =\sqrt{(3a)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(3a)^{2}} & =|3a| \\  & =|3|\cdot |a| \\  & =3|a|\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{x^2} = |x|
$$

Also, we notice that $16$ and $y^2$ are both perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{16{y}^{2}} & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}\cdot {y}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot 4\cdot y\cdot y} \\  & =\sqrt{4\cdot y\cdot 4\cdot y} \\  & =\sqrt{4y\cdot 4y} \\  & =\sqrt{(4y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{(4y)^{2}} & =|4y| \\  & =|4|\cdot |y| \\  & =4|y|\end{aligned}
$$

                    Simplifying a Square Root of a Perfect Square Containing a Fraction
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Remember that the square root of a perfect square can be simplified using absolute value.

$$
\sqrt{x^2} = |x|
$$

Also, we notice that $4, x^2,$ and $y^2$ are all perfect squares.

First, we write the expression under the square root as a perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{\frac{4{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}}} & =\sqrt{\frac{{2}^{2}{x}^{2}}{{y}^{2}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2\cdot 2\cdot x\cdot x}{y\cdot y}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2\cdot x\cdot 2\cdot x}{y\cdot y}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{2x}{y}\cdot \frac{2x}{y}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(\frac{2x}{y})}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we take the absolute value of the squared quantity and simplify using the rules of absolute value:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{(\frac{2x}{y})}^{2}} & =|\frac{2x}{y}| \\  & =\frac{|2x|}{|y|} \\  & =\frac{|2|\cdot |x|}{|y|} \\  & =\frac{2|x|}{|y|}\end{aligned}
$$

tutorials.name: Introduction
tutorials.problem:
When simplifying an algebraic expression involving square roots, it's useful to remember that

$$
\sqrt{x^2} = |x|.
$$

It's tempting to think that $\sqrt{x^2}$ is equivalent to $x,$ but that's not true because $\sqrt{x^2}$ is always non-negative, even if $x$ is negative.

To illustrate, let's evaluate $\sqrt{x^2}$ for a couple of different values of $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{4}^{2}} & =\sqrt{16}=4 \\ \sqrt{(-4)^{2}} & =\sqrt{16}=4\end{aligned}
$$

In both cases, using absolute value gives the correct result:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{{4}^{2}}=|4| & =4 & ✓ \\ \sqrt{(-4)^{2}}=|-4| & =4 & ✓\end{aligned}
$$
